Treating the 809 .unwrap() count as a production-code smell

label: rust-anything is a single-package crate with no workspace: [package] at Cargo.toml:1, edition 2024 at :4, rust-version 1.97 at :8, and no [workspace] table anywhere.

The lint policy is two lines: [lints.rust] unsafe_code = forbid at Cargo.toml:42-43 and [lints.clippy] all = { level = warn, priority = -1 } at :45-46, where priority -1 lets a later specific entry override the group.

sk-code contradicts itself on deny versus forbid: toolchain-and-project-structure.md:61 sets unsafe_code = deny, build-and-organization.md:102 says use deny not forbid, and toolchain-and-project-structure.md:196 opens its example with #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; rust-anything's forbid at Cargo.toml:43 matches line 196.

The finish gate is four commands plus a documentation obligation: CLAUDE.md:6-7 names cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test, and updating docs/STATUS.md when what works changed; hk.pkl:7-15 wires fmt --check and clippy --all-targets --quiet -- -D warnings as pre-commit steps.

sk-code's gate is a flag superset of rust-anything's (adds --locked, cargo check, rustdoc and a release build at build-and-organization.md:122-127 and :131) but has no status-document update obligation and no pre-commit hook wiring.

Error handling is one anyhow funnel with a two-code exit contract: fn main() -> ExitCode matches run() -> Result<ExitCode>, the Err arm prints error: {e:#} and returns ExitCode::from(2) at main.rs:824-834, while a check that ran and failed returns ExitCode::FAILURE at main.rs:1393-1394.

sk-code has no exit-code contract: ExitCode appears in zero files under references/rust/ and assets/checklists/rust-checklist/, and the phrase exit code appears in one, so a CLI cannot tell the tool-broke code from the check-failed code.

unwrap is confined to test modules by discipline, not by a lint: exactly one .unwrap() sits before the first #[cfg(test)] line across all src/*.rs (error_paths.rs), against 809 in total once test modules count, and rust-anything enables only clippy all = warn.
sk-code already covers unwrap discipline and is stricter than rust-anything: unwrap_used, expect_used and panic are all deny at build-and-organization.md:85-87, which rust-anything does not enable.

serde is configured for bit-exact round-tripping: serde_json carries float_roundtrip, preserve_order and unbounded_depth at Cargo.toml:29, with the comment on :28 that recorded floats must survive parsing bit for bit.
Across src/ there are 152 #[serde(...)] attributes, dominated by default plus skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none and Vec::is_empty, plus rename where a Rust keyword collides with a wire name.

sk-code never names the serde_json features that make a recorded value survive a round trip: float_roundtrip and preserve_order appear in zero files under references/rust/ and assets/checklists/rust-checklist/, although serde_json appears in seven.

The crate root is a flat module list and exposes its MSRV to code: src/lib.rs:10-79 is 68 consecutive pub mod lines with three exceptions (#[cfg(test)] mod js_number at :55-56, private mod mime at :62, and the three nesting directories src/lang, src/ts and src/package), while :8 defines pub(crate) const MIN_RUST as env!(CARGO_PKG_RUST_VERSION) and :6 sets #![recursion_limit = 256].

sk-code's layout rules stop at the file boundary: the section-order table at toolchain-and-project-structure.md:104-112 governs dividers inside one file and says nothing about how a crate root lists modules, when a module earns a directory, or how to expose the declared MSRV to code.

The clap CLI is derive-only and pushes every closed set into a ValueEnum: #[derive(Parser)] with name/version/about/after_help at main.rs:25-31, #[derive(Subcommand)] with doc comments as help at :52-72, ValueEnum at :37-50, value_parser = absolute at :111 and allow_hyphen_values at :137.
sk-code says nothing about clap, ratatui or crossterm: each appears in zero files under references/rust/ and assets/checklists/rust-checklist/.

A CLI that writes to stdout must survive a closed pipe, and rust-anything does it with the say! and say_raw! macros at main.rs:6-17, which discard the write result so rust-anything ... | head stops quietly.
sk-code has no broken-pipe rule: broken pipe and SIGPIPE appear in zero files under references/rust/ and assets/checklists/rust-checklist/.

The test tree is 44 integration files plus a shared helper that turns a missing runtime into a skip or a failure on request: tests/common/mod.rs:7 has #![allow(dead_code)], :11-17 reads RUST_ANYTHING_REQUIRE, :34-41 asserts when required and otherwise prints skipped, and fixtures live under tests/fixtures/ in 30-plus per-language directories.

sk-code covers the test file layout but not the skip-versus-fail decision: build-and-organization.md:163-164 matches rust-anything's tests/*.rs and tests/common/mod.rs exactly, and nothing in the set says how a test needing an absent external runtime should behave.

direction: Reading src/main.rs end to end (2227 lines) to characterise the CLI
reason: The derive attributes at 25-50 and the main/run split at 824-834 carry the contract; the rest repeats the same say! and ExitCode pattern per subcommand.

direction: Treating the 809 .unwrap() count as a production-code smell
reason: Splitting at each file's first #[cfg(test)] line reduced it to one, so the raw count was a measurement artefact.
